title: Harrow Viaduct
setting: A night sleeper from Gram to Lorne, crossing a viaduct at two in the morning

victim.name: Ansel Corbin
victim.summary: Railway auditor, missing from cabin five and found below Harrow Viaduct.

brief: Ansel Corbin boarded the Meridian Night Sleeper at Gram. At dawn his cabin was empty and the bed untouched. A track crew found him below Harrow Viaduct. Five people were awake or within reach of car four that night.

suspects.name: Tilda Reeve
suspects.alibi: Says she tended cabins and answered bells until dawn.

suspects.name: Dr. Osric Pell
suspects.relation: Sat across from Ansel at dinner
suspects.alibi: Says he was in his own cabin until a call for help.

suspects.name: Ivo Sandre
suspects.relation: Ran the train and held the crew keys
suspects.alibi: Says he stamped manifests alone in the guard van.

suspects.name: Calla Wren
suspects.relation: Sold brake parts to the line Ansel audited
suspects.alibi: Says she lay in cabin seven with a migraine.

suspects.name: Bram Okafor
suspects.relation: Argued with Ansel over a sacked friend
suspects.alibi: Says he sat up in cabin three with his bad hip.

items.title: Who was aboard
items.body: Crew on duty: Ivo Sandre (conductor), Tilda Reeve (car attendant), one dining steward asleep off duty. Passengers in cars three to five: Dr. Osric Pell, Calla Wren, Bram Okafor, and Ansel Corbin in cabin five. Sleeping cars were locked to the dining car and van after eleven.

lines.q: What did you do for Mr. Corbin that night?
lines.a: He rang at a quarter to one for a milk toddy. I made it in the pantry and set it on the hatch at half past one.

lines.q: Why on the hatch?
lines.a: I had no honey left. I went up to the dining car for a jar. The conductor leaned in at the hatch to talk while I fetched it. I was gone five minutes.

lines.q: Did you notice anything about the crew that morning?
lines.a: Mr. Sandre's coat had lost a brass button at the cuff. He said it caught on a latch. I did not think about it again.

lines.q: Where were you at a quarter past two?
lines.a: Cabin seven. Miss Wren rang with a migraine and the doctor was already there. I stayed with them until twenty-five past.

lines.q: Did you see Mr. Corbin after dinner?
lines.a: No. We spoke over soup. He said he had a long night of paperwork.

lines.q: Your sleeping tablets were reported missing. When did you notice?
lines.a: Before we left Gram. At the platform I turned and found my case open. I told the station master at ten to ten.

lines.q: Who handled your bag?
lines.a: I bought a paper while the conductor carried it up to my car. Then I counted my strips.

lines.q: Where were you at a quarter past two?
lines.a: In cabin seven. Miss Wren sent for me. I stayed at her bedside.

lines.q: Where were you between half past one and three?
lines.a: In the guard van, stamping manifests. Alone. It is dull work and I do it every night.

lines.q: Who holds the crew door cards?
lines.a: Three cards. Mine, the attendant's, and a spare sealed in the van safe. Mine stays on my belt.

lines.q: Did you see anyone near car four?
lines.a: Mr. Okafor, earlier. He was pacing the corridor with his cane, angry about Corbin. I sent him back to his cabin.

lines.q: The attendant says you lost a button.
lines.a: A latch caught my cuff. It happens on old stock.

lines.q: How did you know Mr. Corbin?
lines.a: My firm sells brake parts to the line. He audited our invoices. We were not friends.

lines.q: Where were you at a quarter past two?
lines.a: Cabin seven, flat on my back with a migraine. The doctor came, then the attendant with water.

lines.q: Did you hear anything?
lines.a: A gust of cold air, a banging. It went on for a minute. I thought a window was open.

lines.q: Did either of them leave?
lines.a: Neither. The doctor held my wrist. The attendant left a little after twenty past two.

lines.q: What was your quarrel with Mr. Corbin?
lines.a: He wrote a report that got my friend sacked. I told him so at dinner. I said nothing more.

lines.q: Where were you at a quarter past two?
lines.a: Cabin three. My hip was bad. I sat up with the light on.

lines.q: Could you reach car four's far door?
lines.a: I could walk to the car four corridor. The outer door needs a crew card. I have never held one.

lines.q: Did you give Mr. Corbin a drink?
lines.a: I bought him a brandy at dinner. He left it. That was all.

sections.heading: Found
sections.body: At first light, a man lay on the embankment below the central pier. A single leather slipper lay on the ballast beside him.

sections.heading: Scene
sections.body: No tracks other than the crew's. Nothing on the rails above. The viaduct rail is intact.

sections.heading: Note
sections.body: The outer door between cars four and five was latched when the train reached Lorne.

sections.heading: Cause
sections.body: Injuries consistent with a fall from a moving train at speed.

sections.heading: Bloods
sections.body: Heavy sedative present: somnex, a prescription sleeping agent. No sign of struggle on the hands or arms.

sections.heading: Stomach
sections.body: Milk and a trace of honey. He had taken the sedative within an hour of death.

sections.heading: Pads
sections.body: Front pads measured below the legal limit at the last depot stop. Re-measure ordered.

sections.heading: Certificate
sections.body: Brake certificate 4417 shows the Dunmore depot stamp. Dunmore depot closed that month for flooding.

sections.heading: Countersign
sections.body: Countersigned in ink by the conductor on duty. Initials: I. S.

items.title: Ansel's audit notebook, torn page
items.body: Carriage four. Four certificates, one stamp, same smudge on every pad. Dunmore stamp dated the month the depot flooded. Someone signs these on the train and the depot never sees them. Tell nobody before Lorne. Name the signer to the board.

items.title: Crew card roster
items.body: C-01 issued to I. Sandre, conductor. A-02 issued to T. Reeve, car attendant. S-03 spare, sealed in the guard van safe. Cards open cabin doors on their own car and the outer doors between cars. Passengers hold cabin keys only.

items.title: Incident slip, Gram station
items.body: 21:50. Dr. O. Pell reports his sleeping tablets missing from a case left open on the platform. Station master noted: eight strips of somnex, taken between the cab rank and car five.

items.title: Copy of brake certificate 4417
items.body: Brake certificate 4417, carriage four. Dunmore depot stamp, smudged at the lower edge. Countersigned in ink, initials I. S. Date line left blank.

rows.text: Car four to five outer door locked automatically.
Sleeping cars locked to passengers. Crew cards only.
Card A-02 opens cabin five door, closes after ninety seconds.
Card A-02 opens cabin seven door.
Car four to five outer door unlocked by card C-01. Held open thirty-eight seconds.
Card A-02 closes cabin seven door.
Spare card S-03 safe seal checked, unbroken.
Quarrel in the dining car between A. Corbin and B. Okafor, steward notes.
Ansel leaves a voicemail for head office.
Cabin five rings for a milk toddy.
Toddy set on the pantry hatch. Attendant leaves for honey.
Wake call. Cabin five found empty.

items.title: Dining car receipt
items.body: 23:05. One brandy, signed to cabin five, ordered by B. Okafor. Untouched when cleared at 23:40. Steward's note: heated words between the two men, no blows.

motives.text: Revenge for a friend sacked after an earlier audit
A debt Ansel was about to call in
Ansel was blocking the sale of the line
Ansel was about to expose forged brake certificates the killer signed
Ansel had seen a stolen cargo loaded at night

methods.text: Pushed through the window of his own cabin
Struck on the head in his cabin and thrown from the train
Sedated in his nightcap, walked to the outer door and pushed out on the viaduct
Poisoned with heart tablets and dropped later
Thrown from the outer door by an emergency brake jolt
